historical_record.description: Digging began about November 1, 1898 on the largest and most northerly of the Chain of Lakes, opposite Fortieth Avenue: 38,000 cubic yards were dug out and piled in natural-looking mounds to the east, and the lake was given seven planted islands and a 30-foot drive around it, with a footpath at the water's edge.

The main lake of the new chain at the west end of the park was finished by mid-1899: fifty-five men with an engine and twelve cars had graded the natural hollow down to a foot below the water table, leaving a lake about 1,500 feet long and 100 to 400 feet wide with a winding shore, a creek-like neck of water to the west, and islands planted with birch and rhododendron, alder and fern, willow and iris, and Louisiana swamp cypress.
